A bruised purple sky hangs low and swollen, pressing down like a wound that refuses to close, leaking sickly amber light along the horizon.
Ash falls in slow curtains from a sky the color of a week-old corpse, the sun somewhere behind it, extinguished and forgotten.
The clouds churn the color of old blood, rolling in from the east like a tide of rot, dragging sulfur-stink and flickering red darkness.
A blackened sun sits motionless overhead, ringed by a halo of diseased green, casting shadows that fall in the wrong directions.
The sky is the color of a bruise pressed too hard, a sickly greenish-yellow mass that breathes and shifts without wind.
Storm-light the color of tarnished copper drowns the valley, the clouds above knotted and muscular, shot through with veins of dead orange.
No stars. No moon. Only a void-purple expanse pressing down, thick and suffocating, broken by distant pulses of pale, sourceless corpse-light.
A sky of churning black smoke and ancient ash, backlit by something burning far below the horizon, casting the world in ember-red.
The thunderheads are the color of iron left to rust in blood, and they have not moved in three days, and they will not.
Pale light seeps through a sky the color of curdled milk, wrongly luminous, too bright in the wrong places, dark where the sun should be.
The sky hangs like a funeral shroud soaked in old rain, sagging and grey-green, dripping something that is not quite water onto the stones.
Sickly yellow-green clouds press the horizon flat, the air beneath them carrying the taste of copper and the smell of extinguished pyres.
A blood-red sky without a single break in the clouds, the light it casts thick and wrong, turning everything beneath it the color of open wounds.
The overcast is absolute, a seamless dark vault of storm-bruised purple-grey, and beneath it the world holds its breath and does not exhale.
Ash-fall thickens the sky to a pale, choking white-grey, and through it the dead sun bleeds a ring of cold, jaundiced light.
The clouds move against the wind, slow and deliberate, their undersides lit by a dim corpse-light that casts no warmth on anything below.
A void opens where the sky should be, not dark but the absence of color entirely, rimmed by sickly green where the world protests its edge.
The storm has been overhead for so long the lightning no longer startles anyone, its bruised purple flashes illuminating nothing but more ruin.
Heavy clouds the color of weeks-old ash sag toward the earth, dragging curtains of dark sleet and the smell of old iron behind them.
The sky is wrong in a way that resists description, a dark amber-brown mass that breathes slowly, the blackened sun pulsing within it like a dying coal.
Corpse-pale light drifts down from a sky the color of a dead man's skin, formless, directionless, casting shadows beneath objects where shadows cannot be.
The horizon is a line of deep arterial red beneath clouds of absolute black, the space between them the color of a killing bruise.
A sickly green overcast devours the sky from edge to edge, and the rain that falls from it is warm and leaves stains the color of bile.
The clouds are the purple-black of a strangled throat, lit from within by irregular pulses of pale light, carrying thunder that sounds like grinding bone.
Nothing above but a collapsing dark, storm-bruised and total, broken only by the dead sun's faint ring of orange rot bleeding through the black.
A bruised, storm-swollen sky pressing down like a fist, livid purple bleeding into sickly yellow at the horizon where nothing good survives.
Ash raining from a sky the color of a dead man's skin, thick grey clouds sealing out every last memory of warmth.
The sun a blackened disc behind roiling smoke, casting red-tinged shadow over everything, turning midday into something worse than night.
Clouds the color of old bruises churning overhead, lit from within by sickly green flickers, the whole sky groaning with held pressure.
Blood-red sky stretched taut and featureless above the blasted plain, neither dawn nor dusk, simply the color the world had become.
A void-black ceiling of cloud so low it scraped the tower spires, smothering the land beneath absolute, suffocating dark.
Corpse-pale light filtering through layers of yellow smoke, casting no true shadows, making the living look already dead.
The sky hemorrhaging deep violet into black, storm-veins of sick amber crackling at the edges where the darkness refused to hold.
Thick curtains of falling ash obscuring the sky entirely, the world reduced to grey above and grey below and nothing between.
A greenish, pestilent sky sagging with the weight of centuries of rot, clouds moving too slowly, too deliberately, like something breathing.
The horizon burning a furious orange-red while overhead the sky collapsed into absolute black, the two halves refusing to reconcile.
Smoke columns rising from distant ruin merging into a permanent dark canopy, erasing the sky and replacing it with something meaner.
Sickly ochre light pressing through fractured storm clouds, each gap bleeding a different wrong color, the sky unable to decide how to die.
A sky the deep purple-black of a three-day bruise, heavy and absolute, the stars long since choked out and forgotten.
Rain falling upward in places, the storm-dark sky broken and misbehaving, clouds torn into ragged shapes that suggested mouths, suggested teeth.
The blackened sun hanging overhead like a wound that refused to close, radiating cold instead of warmth across the scorched land.
Layers of grey and charcoal cloud stacked to impossible heights, the whole mass rotating slowly, a grinding sky-engine producing nothing but dread.
Pale corpse-light bleeding sideways from the west, the sky not glowing so much as refusing to fully darken, trapped in something worse.
A sky thick with iron-grey cloud torn at irregular intervals to reveal not sky but deeper dark, as though something hollow waited above.
Storm light the color of infected flesh washing across everything, the clouds overhead split and weeping trails of black rain.
Void-purple sky pressing flat against the mountaintops, motionless and absolute, the kind of sky that had never once seen sunrise.
The atmosphere choked with particulate and smoke, the sun reduced to a smear of dull red that provided light but no comfort.
Roiling black and deep crimson clouds locked together overhead, lit from somewhere below by the glow of things that should not burn.
A sick, greenish-yellow cast to the entire sky, the light wrong in a fundamental way, making wounds look deeper and faces look hollow.
The sky a permanent, featureless slab of dark grey, neither storming nor clearing, simply refusing to be sky at all anymore.
Storm-bruised heavens choked with rolling black clouds, sickly green light bleeding through the gaps where thunder growls without ceasing.
Ash-fall sky, grey and suffocating, thick flakes drifting down like the remains of something vast and holy burned away forever.
Blood-red ceiling pressing low over cracked earth, veins of deeper crimson pulsing slowly as if the sky itself still breathes.
The sun a blackened disc, ringed in poisoned amber, casting no warmth across the dead fields stretching endlessly below.
Void-purple darkness absolute above, broken only by slow-moving columns of black smoke rising from distant fires that never die.
Corpse-light pale and sickly, the sky offering illumination without source, a flat dead glow that strips all shadow of comfort.
Bruised yellows and rotting greens seething overhead, clouds churning in slow malevolent spirals around a sky that forgot what calm was.
The heavens the colour of an old wound, deep purple-brown and festering, clouds hanging motionless like clotted flesh above the wastes.
Perpetual twilight the colour of rusted iron, horizon glowing faintly where something burned days ago and still refuses to stop burning.
Black sky split by dry lightning that never reaches ground, illuminating briefly a ceiling of clouds built like stacked funeral stones.
Sickly amber haze pressing down, thick as oil smoke, the sun reduced to a smear of orange rot behind the murk.
The sky a bruised eye, swollen purple fading to black at the zenith, weeping cold rain that smells faintly of copper.
Ash-grey and absolute, every cloud the same dead colour, the world above offering nothing but slow suffocation dressed as weather.
Blood-dark overcast from edge to edge, no break, no seam, a single vast wound sealed shut above the blighted landscape.
Greenish-black storm wall advancing without wind, the light beneath it turning flesh to the colour of drowned things long underwater.
The sun ringed in black, its face sickly and diminished, throwing pale diseased light across a sky the colour of bruises.
Corpse-pale luminescence diffused through every cloud, sourceless and cold, the sky giving light the way dead men give warmth.
Rolling black thunderheads lit from within by deep red pulses, the whole mass groaning as it grinds across the poisoned firmament.
Void above and void below, the sky a perfect darkness broken only by slow curtains of grey ash drifting without wind.
Sickly green light saturating the underbelly of churning clouds, the colour of old plague, of marshwater, of something sacred gone wrong.
The heavens the shade of old iron left in rain, flat and lightless, pressing down on the broken towers below.
Purple-black and vast, the storm refusing to break, lightning trapped inside the clouds, illuminating their bellies in brief silent agony.
Dried-blood red from north to south, the sky offering no gradient, no variation, only the one unbearable colour held without mercy.
Pale as a cataract, the sky seeing nothing clearly, its cold dead light turning every surface the colour of old bone.
Black sun hanging at false noon, its corona a sickly ring of brown-gold, the world beneath receiving only the memory of light.
A bruised purple sky pressing low over the dead fields, swollen with unshed rain, the horizon hemorrhaging dark crimson where the sun drowned hours ago.
Ash-choked heavens the color of a corpse's pallor, shedding grey flakes that settle like snow on the cracked earth below, silent and suffocating.

Blackened sun hanging motionless behind layers of smoke, casting no warmth, only a diseased amber smear across the belly of the oppressive clouds above.
Storm-bruised firmament churning in shades of old blood and charcoal, the clouds rolling inward like a fist closing slowly over the ruined landscape below.
A void-dark canopy stretched taut and featureless, the absence of stars more terrifying than darkness itself, the sky simply gone, replaced by crushing nothing.
Corpse-light pale sky, the luminescence sourceless and wrong, every shadow falling the incorrect direction, the light arriving from no sun, no moon, no fire.
Crimson-streaked heavens like a battlefield ceiling, the clouds torn and ragged at their edges, bleeding upward into a deep and lightless arterial darkness above.

A sickly ochre dome of sky, the color of infected wounds, the clouds stationary and bloated, hanging as if gorged on something dark and vast below.
Void-purple darkness eating the horizon from all sides inward, the last pale center of sky shrinking, the world being swallowed from its edges first.
Storm clouds the color of old iron grinding slowly across the sky, their undersides lit in pulses of sickly red from fires burning far below.
The heavens entirely bruise-dark, no break in the cloud cover for days, the pressure of the sky something felt behind the eyes, inside the teeth.
Blood-red dawn that never resolves into day, the light stalled and lurid, painting everything the color of aftermath, of ruin already accomplished and cooling.
A ceiling of churning black cloud threaded through with veins of deep violet, the whole mass rotating almost imperceptibly, patient, slow, and unmistakably alive.
Corpse-pale sky emitting cold white luminescence through cloud thick as wool, the glow sourceless and accusatory, bleaching all color from the world beneath it.
Sickly green light filtering through smoke-clouds stained with sulfur, the sky tinted the shade of standing water in a plague-touched city long abandoned.
The sun a blackened disc, visible but offering nothing, a hole in the grey sky that absorbs rather than radiates, surrounded by a halo of ash.
Heavy storm-bruised clouds hanging unmoving for three days, their color deepening from charcoal to something between purple and rot, the air below them impossibly still.
A sky scraped raw and red, the clouds shredded into long parallel streaks like claw marks across the belly of heaven, all of it bleeding light downward.
Ash-fall without wind, the grey particles descending vertically and endlessly from a sky the color of old pewter, coating the world in a fine funereal grey.
The horizon glowing a deep malevolent amber, not sunrise, not sunset, something burning far away and vast, the sky above it darkening from brown to black.
Void-dark sky in which even the clouds are invisible, the world existing under pure oppressive absence, the occasional lightning flash revealing nothing comforting in the dark above.
